your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: Rejecting p2's offer of $100 for Kentucky Avenue. First, its mortgage value alone is $110. More importantly, p2 owns Indiana and p3 owns Illinois—if I give p2 Kentucky, p2 can buy Illinois from p3, giving p2 the Red monopoly and giving p3 the cash they desperately need to build houses on Yellow. Holding Kentucky blocks Red and starves p3 of trade liquidity.
I only have $46 cash and the minimum next bid is $151, so I must drop out. Having p4 or p2 take Pennsylvania Avenue at a discount and block p3 (who owns Pacific Avenue) is great for me.

I have $18 cash and am on Pennsylvania Avenue, just 6 steps from GO. I can hold Kentucky Avenue unmortgaged for now and only mortgage it for $110 if I need cash later. Meanwhile, p2 (on Pacific), p3 (on Pennsylvania), and p4 (on Atlantic) are all approaching my developed Dark Blue monopoly (Park Place with 2 houses, Boardwalk with 3 houses). Ending turn.

Holding $218 cash and unmortgaged Kentucky Avenue ($110 mortgage value) as a buffer before crossing p4's Light Blue monopoly (rents $400-$450). Once I safely pass Connecticut Avenue, I can invest in building the 3rd house on Park Place. Ending turn.

Building a 3rd house on Park Place for $200, jumping its rent from $500 to $1,100. This leaves me with $368 cash plus $110 mortgageable on Kentucky Avenue ($478 total liquidity without touching houses), which covers even the 1-in-36 roll of 2 onto Connecticut Avenue ($450 rent) and leaves cash to buy unowned properties ahead.
I have 3 houses on both Park Place and Boardwalk ($1,100 and $1,400 rent) and $368 cash remaining. Keeping this cash to buy unowned properties ahead and maintain a safety buffer. Ending turn.
Safely past Light Blue with $318 cash. Keeping cash to buy unowned properties ahead (Virginia, New York, B&O, North Carolina) and cover p3's Yellow rents. Ending turn.
Holding $304 cash to buy unowned properties ahead (B&O Railroad, North Carolina Avenue) and cover p3's Yellow rents, since no opponents are currently near Park Place or Boardwalk. Ending turn.
Keeping $284 cash to buy unowned properties ahead (B&O Railroad, North Carolina Avenue) and cover p3's Yellow rents, as no opponents are in range of Dark Blue this round. Ending turn.

p4 is on B&O Railroad (within dice roll of 12 to Park Place, and next turn right through Dark Blue). I am on Short Line, about to pass GO and cross p4's Light Blue monopoly ($400-$450 rent). However, there are only 8 houses left in the bank, and 3rd->4th house on Boardwalk increases rent from $1,400 to $1,700 (enough to completely bankrupt p4). Wait—if I build 1 house on Boardwalk for $200, I'll have $84 cash + $110 mortgageable on Kentucky = $194, plus if I pass GO on my next roll (anything 5 or higher from Short Line passes GO!), I get $200 cash -> $394 + $110 = $504, which easily covers Light Blue! Only a roll of 2, 3, or 4 doesn't pass GO immediately, and none of those hit Light Blue anyway! So building 1 house on Boardwalk now is 100% safe against Light Blue and locks up another house from the bank while boosting Boardwalk rent to $1,700.
